## Background

[curatedMetagenomicData](https://waldronlab.io/curatedMetagenomicData/) (cMD)
is a collection of human shotgun metagenomes from published studies, every
sample processed through the same pipeline and paired with curated sample
metadata, so that profiles from different studies can be compared and pooled.
Each sample's raw reads are quality-controlled and profiled with MetaPhlAn
(taxonomic relative abundance), Kraken2/Bracken, a resistome screen against
CARD and, in some pipeline configurations, HUMAnN (functional profiles).

The profiles are now published as open **data releases** at
<https://cmgd-public.cancerdatasci.org>. The layout has a few concepts that
the rest of this vignette relies on:

-   A **dataset** is one pipeline registration: a pipeline version together with
    its configuration, named `<workflow_id>-<version>`, for example
    `cmgd_mpa4.2-2.3.0` (pipeline 2.3.0, MetaPhlAn 4.2, no HUMAnN). Profiles
    from different datasets were made with different tools or databases and
    are kept apart.
-   A **release** is an immutable, full snapshot of a dataset, named by its UTC
    build date (`2026-10-16`). A release never changes once published; new data
    arrive as a new release. Cite the dataset and the release id.
-   Each release has a **manifest** (`manifest.json`) listing its **tables**
    (long, tidy tables such as `taxonomic_profile_metaphlan` or `qc_metrics`,
    stored as Parquet files), ready-made **per-study files**, and a read-only
    [DuckLake](https://ducklake.select) catalog that lets DuckDB query the
    whole release in place.
-   Every file is listed with its size and SHA-256 checksum. cmgdr downloads
    files into a local **cache** and verifies them against those checksums; a
    file that does not verify is deleted and an error raised. Because releases
    are immutable, a cached file never goes stale.

The site cannot be listed like a directory: everything is found through JSON
indexes, which is what cmgdr reads.

cmgdr is deliberately a low-level client. It knows the published layout
and returns plain data frames, lists, local file paths, a DuckDB connection,
and (for convenience) a species `TreeSummarizedExperiment`. It does not
reshape, join or model the data; higher-level packages are expected to build
on it.

This vignette uses the small `cmgd_mpa4.2-2.3.0` release (125 samples in 8
studies) and, within it, the three-sample `ZellerG_2014` study, so it
downloads only a few hundred kilobytes. All code runs against the live site.

## Setup

cmgdr is not on Bioconductor yet. Install it from GitHub; once it is accepted,
`BiocManager::install("cmgdr")` will work.

```{r}
#| label: install
#| eval: false
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("seandavi/cmgdr")
```

Downloads go to `cmgd_cache_dir()`, which is
`tools::R_user_dir("cmgdr", "cache")` and moves with the `R_USER_CACHE_DIR`
environment variable. This vignette points it at a temporary directory so
building it leaves nothing behind.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(cmgdr)
Sys.setenv(R_USER_CACHE_DIR = tempfile("cmgdr-cache"))
cmgd_cache_dir()
```

## Finding datasets and releases

`cmgd_datasets()` takes no required arguments (only `base`, the site URL) and
returns a data frame with one row per published dataset: its id
(`dataset`), the pipeline registration it comes from (`workflow_id`,
`version`), and the id of its newest release (`latest`).

```{r}
#| label: datasets
datasets <- cmgd_datasets()
datasets
```

`cmgd_releases()` takes a dataset id and returns one row per release of
that dataset, oldest first: the release id, its build date, when it was
published, and whether it is `pinned` (kept as a long-term reference).

```{r}
#| label: releases
cmgd_releases("cmgd_mpa4.2-2.3.0")
```

`cmgd_release()` opens a release. It takes a dataset id and a release id; the
default `release = "latest"` resolves to the newest one, but for reproducible
work pin the id, as here. It reads the release's manifest and returns a
`cmgd_release` object, the handle every other cmgdr function takes. It is a
list with the dataset and release ids, the release URL and the parsed
manifest; printing it shows the tables it holds.

```{r}
#| label: release
rel <- cmgd_release("cmgd_mpa4.2-2.3.0", release = "2026-10-16")
rel
class(rel)
names(rel$manifest)
```

## Tables and files

`cmgd_tables()` takes a release and returns one row per table: its `name`,
a `description`, its `grain` (what one row of the table means), its
`row_count`, and its `license`. Most tables are CC0-1.0; tables that include
values derived from the Olm lab Microbiome Repo are CC-BY-4.0 (see
[Sample metadata](#sample-metadata)).

```{r}
#| label: tables
tables <- cmgd_tables(rel)
tables[, c("name", "grain", "row_count", "license")]
```

A table is stored as one or more Parquet files. `cmgd_files()` takes a release
and, optionally, table names, and returns one row per file: the `table`, the
file's `path` relative to the release, its full `url`, its `size` in bytes,
its `sha256`, and the number of `rows` it holds.

```{r}
#| label: files
files <- cmgd_files(rel, "qc_metrics")
str(files)
```

`cmgd_download()` takes a release and one path (as in the `path` column) or
full URL, downloads the file into the cache, verifies its size and SHA-256,
and returns the local file path. Calling it again returns the cached copy
without downloading, as long as the copy still verifies.

```{r}
#| label: download
local <- cmgd_download(rel, files$path[1])
local
file.size(local) == files$size[1]
```

## Studies

Besides whole tables, each release has ready-made files for each study.
`cmgd_studies()` takes a release and returns one row per study: its
`study_name` and `n_samples`.

```{r}
#| label: studies
studies <- cmgd_studies(rel)
studies
```

`cmgd_study_files()` takes a release and a study name and returns one row
per file published for that study: its `name`, `path`, `url`, `size`,
`sha256` and a `description` of what it holds. There is a species × samples
matrix (`metaphlan_species.tsv.gz`), the study's rows of the main tables as
Parquet, and a QC table (`qc.tsv`).

```{r}
#| label: study-files
study_files <- cmgd_study_files(rel, "ZellerG_2014")
study_files[, c("name", "size")]
```

`cmgd_read_study()` takes a release, a study and the file's `name` without
extension (`"qc"`, `"metaphlan"`, `"bracken"`, `"metaphlan_species"`, ...),
downloads it through the verified cache and reads it into a data frame.
Parquet files are read with the duckdb package. The QC table has one row per
sample: its keys (`sample_key`, `readset_id`, `run_ids`), read and base counts
before and after decontamination, and the pipeline version and commit that
produced it.

```{r}
#| label: read-study
qc <- cmgd_read_study(rel, "ZellerG_2014", "qc")
str(qc)
```

## A species TreeSummarizedExperiment

`cmgd_species_tse()` takes a release and a study and builds a
`TreeSummarizedExperiment` from the study's species matrix. Rows are MetaPhlAn
species clades (full `k__...|s__...` names), columns are samples
(`sample_key`), and the one assay, `relative_abundance`, is a sparse matrix of
percentages from the main MetaPhlAn pass on all reads. The QC table above is
its `colData`.

```{r}
#| label: species-tse
tse <- cmgd_species_tse(rel, "ZellerG_2014")
tse
abundance <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(tse, "relative_abundance")
class(abundance)
# Shorten the clade names to the species for display
rownames(abundance) <- sub(".*\\|s__", "", rownames(abundance))
top <- order(-Matrix::rowSums(abundance))[1:5]
as.matrix(abundance[top, ])
```

## Sample metadata {#sample-metadata}

Releases since `cmgd_mpa4.2-2.3.0` / `2026-10-16` publish sample metadata as
tables. `cmgd_sample_metadata()` takes a release, a `source`, optional
`study` names and `wide`, and returns a data frame. The sources are:

-   `harmonized` (the default): one value per sample and harmonized field,
    taken from the cMD curation where it has one and from the Olm lab
    Microbiome Repo otherwise. CC-BY-4.0.
-   `cmd`: the curatedMetagenomicData curation as published. CC0-1.0.
-   `olm`: the Olm lab Microbiome Repo, with its route and confidence.
    CC-BY-4.0.

With `wide = FALSE` (the default) the table comes back long, as published:
one row per sample and field, with the `value`, the `source` it came
from, the source's `release`, and for Olm values the `route` and
`confidence`.

```{r}
#| label: metadata-long
meta <- cmgd_sample_metadata(rel, study = "ZellerG_2014")
head(meta)
```

Reading a CC-BY-4.0 table prints a message naming the licence and the DOI to
cite. The licence and the pinned source releases the table was built from
(with their DOIs and checksums) are also attached as attributes, so they
travel with the data:

```{r}
#| label: metadata-attribution
attr(meta, "license")
attr(meta, "sources")[, c("source", "release", "doi", "license")]
```

If you use the `harmonized` or `olm` tables, cite the Microbiome Repo DOI
above as well as curatedMetagenomicData; the
[provenance](#provenance) lists the full citation text.

With `wide = TRUE` the result has one row per sample: the sample's
`study_name`, `sample_key`, `biosample`, `bioproject` and `run_accessions`,
then one character column per field, `NA` where a sample has no value.

```{r}
#| label: metadata-wide
wide <- cmgd_sample_metadata(
    rel,
    source = "cmd", study = "ZellerG_2014", wide = TRUE
)
dim(wide)
wide[, c("sample_key", "biosample", "age_years", "sex", "health_condition")]
```

A release without metadata tables raises an error of class
`cmgdr_no_metadata`, which callers can catch with `tryCatch()`.

## Species profiles for samples picked by metadata

The wide table is a plain data frame with one row per sample, so dplyr verbs
(or base subsetting) pick samples by their metadata, across studies.
`cmgd_samples_tse()` takes the result, or a vector of `sample_key`s, and
builds one species `TreeSummarizedExperiment` for those samples, in that
order. Rows are the union of the studies' species, `0` where a species was
not seen, and `colData` is each sample's `qc.tsv` row followed by its
metadata from `source`. The licence and sources travel in `metadata()`.

```{r}
#| label: samples-tse
#| message: false
library(dplyr)
picked <- cmgd_sample_metadata(rel, wide = TRUE) |>
    filter(health_condition == "case", sex == "female")
count(picked, study_name)
cases <- cmgd_samples_tse(rel, picked)
cases
cases$study_name |> table()
S4Vectors::metadata(cases)$license
```

## Finding samples by run accession

`cmgd_find_runs()` takes a release and a vector of SRA/ENA run accessions
(`SRR...`, `ERR...`, `DRR...`) and looks them up in the release's `samples`
table, where a sample's runs are `;`-joined. It returns a data frame with one
row per accession, in the order given: the `run`, then the matching
`samples` row (study, `sample_key`, BioSample, BioProject, pipeline version,
...). A run the release does not have gets a row of `NA`s, so the result
always lines up with the input.

```{r}
#| label: find-runs
runs <- cmgd_find_runs(rel, c("ERR478962", "SRR0000000"))
runs[, c("run", "study_name", "sample_key", "biosample", "bioproject")]
```

## Provenance {#provenance}

`cmgd_provenance()` takes a release and returns its `provenance.json` as a
list: the lake snapshots the release was built from
(`source_asset_versions`) and, for releases since `2026-10-16`, a `cmgd`
section with the pipeline registration (repository, revision, parameters),
the pipeline runs, the reference database versions, the pinned metadata
sources, the licence of every table, and citation text.

```{r}
#| label: provenance
prov <- cmgd_provenance(rel)
names(prov$cmgd)
str(prov$cmgd$databases)
prov$cmgd$pipeline_runs
prov$cmgd$citation
```

## Whole tables with SQL and dplyr

`cmgd_connect()` takes a release and returns a DBI connection to an
in-memory DuckDB database with the release's DuckLake catalog attached
read-only. Every table in `cmgd_tables()` is available by name. Nothing is
downloaded up front: DuckDB fetches only the parts of the remote Parquet files
a query needs.

```{r}
#| label: connect
con <- cmgd_connect(rel)
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
    SELECT study_name, count(*) AS n_samples,
        avg(reads_decontaminated) AS mean_reads
    FROM qc_metrics
    GROUP BY study_name
    ORDER BY n_samples DESC")
```

The same connection works with dplyr (and dbplyr). Here are the five most
abundant species in `ZellerG_2014`, averaged over its samples. A species
missing from a sample has no row, so divide by the study's sample count rather
than taking a mean.

```{r}
#| label: dplyr
#| message: false
library(dplyr)
n <- tbl(con, "qc_metrics") |>
    filter(study_name == "ZellerG_2014") |>
    count() |>
    pull(n)
tbl(con, "taxonomic_profile_metaphlan") |>
    filter(
        study_name == "ZellerG_2014", rank == "species",
        data_type == "full_data", is.na(humann_bundle)
    ) |>
    group_by(clade_name) |>
    summarise(mean_percent = sum(relative_abundance, na.rm = TRUE) / n) |>
    arrange(desc(mean_percent)) |>
    head(5) |>
    collect() |>
    mutate(species = sub(".*\\|s__", "", clade_name), .keep = "unused")
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
```

Before computing across tables:

1.  Abundances from different methods are not on the same scale. MetaPhlAn
    `relative_abundance` is a percent; Bracken `fraction_total_reads` is a 0–1
    fraction.
2.  Pick one `data_type`, either `full_data` (all reads) or `rarefied_data` (a
    1M-read subsample). Most analyses want `full_data`.
3.  Pick one MetaPhlAn pass. In HUMAnN datasets the bundle's own MetaPhlAn
    pass (`humann_bundle` set) sits next to the main pass
    (`humann_bundle IS NULL`).

Each release's `README.md` and `tables/<table>/schema.json` document every
column.

## HUMAnN gene families

HUMAnN datasets (`cmgd_humann3.9-2.3.0`, `cmgd_humann4a1-2.3.0`) also publish
per-sample HUMAnN gene-family tables. These are too large for the release
tables, so each is its own download from
`https://cmgd-raw.cancerdatasci.org`, listed in the release's gene-family
index. `cmgd_genefamilies()` takes a release and returns
one row per study with gene families; with `study`, one row per file with its
`url`, `size`, `sha256` and row count, which `cmgd_download()` fetches and
verifies. No HUMAnN dataset is on the public site yet, so this code is shown
but not run.

```{r}
#| label: genefamilies
#| eval: false
gf_rel <- cmgd_release("cmgd_humann3.9-2.3.0")
cmgd_genefamilies(gf_rel)
gf <- cmgd_genefamilies(gf_rel, study = "ZellerG_2014")
path <- cmgd_download(gf_rel, gf$url[1])
genefamilies <- read.delim(path, check.names = FALSE)
```

sessionInfo()
